Add support for UPDATE statements that update distribution column. 
Due to distributed nature, such statements should be executed cross-shard. Old tuples from UPDATE source (WHERE clause) should become deleted, while new tuples should be inserted on destination shard.
To achieve this, use SPQR multi-slice infrastructure introduced in previous commits.  
For such update's SPQR planner will create "split-insert" plan. This will be typically 3-slice plan, including two inner slices that transfers tuples between shards, using BINARY COPY PostgreSQL feature, and top-level slice, which will update tuples on destination shard  once transferred.

Refactor Session Parameter handling + Tests (#2238)

Session parameter handler stores parameter changes as a stack of actions `SET` or `RESET`. Each change has a TX count and a value that was set. TX count is incremented on `BEGIN` and `SAVEPOINT` commands.
When `COMMIT` is executed, last non-`LOCAL` change is applied and stack is truncated until TX count 0, which represents changes made outside the transaction block. 
When `ROLLBACK` is executed, stack is truncated and then last non-`LOCAL` value is set. 

Virtual parameters did not follow these behavior from the beginning, so they were left unchanged according to the logic.
